question: Presbyopia occurs primarily because the crystalline lens gradually loses its elasticity with age, reducing the amplitude of accommodation — it is not primarily due to weakening of the ciliary muscle.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Ciliary muscle function is relatively preserved in presbyopia; the primary defect is lens sclerosis (loss of elasticity), which prevents adequate curvature change during accommodation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The lens nucleus becomes progressively sclerotic (harder) from the fourth decade, so even when ciliary muscle contracts and zonules relax, the lens cannot change curvature sufficiently to increase its power for near vision.
